item.title: Mina Kimes assigns blame for the Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy controversy
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Aaron Rodgers’ controversial comments about Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy drew all sorts of reactions online, but they probably shouldn’t have come as the biggest surprise, considering their tenure together with the Green Bay Packers also ended poorly, albeit in a much less public manner. Their reunion lasted 10 games before the Steelers released a shocking statement late Tuesday night announcing Rodgers had been benched and wouldn’t play in this week’s game. Rodgers went scorched earth on Wednesday’s episode of The Pat McAfee Show , accusing McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep during team meetings, alluding to the Steelers’ head coach struggling to keep up with the rigors of coaching an NFL team, and maintaining that the coach held a grudge against him from how things ended in Green Bay. Following Rodgers tell-all, McCarthy danced around the accusations and asserted that he is still the right man to lead the franchise. Reports emerged that suggested that Rodgers gave Pittsburgh an ultimatum over play-calling responsibilities , and the franchise called him on it, resultin in his benching. Rodgers has received the lion’s share of the blame for airing out his dirty laundry in a public manner, but ESPN’s Mina Kimes, at least, thinks that the Steelers should have seen this coming. “The Steelers organization is the one who deserves the most blame. The front office and ownership,” Kimes said. “It was all so god damn predictable. That’s what I’ll say. Everybody was shocked when this reunion happened cause we all knew they didn’t like each other.” Kimes added that “the football was also very predictable,” noting that Rodgers and the Steelers offense were putting up league-worst numbers. “It’s not like the Steelers didn’t know any of this,” she continued. “They made a terrible football decision, but also a terrible people management decision. And they, to me, deserve more blame than anyone in all this. “This was a disaster entirely of their own making. It was kinda the most predictable ending to all this, and nobody should be surprised… It’s like when you have two friends who are exes who get back together, and every single person in the friend group is like, ‘This is a horrible idea,’ but nobody will say it to their faces.” The post Mina Kimes assigns blame for the Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy controversy appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: AF Corse Expands IMSA GTD Effort For 2027 Season
item.description: A driver navigates the course during the GTP/GTD Pro Practice 1 session for the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship at the Chevrolet Detroit Grand Prix presented by Lear in Detroit on Friday, May 29, 2026. AF Corse is no longer just a guest at the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship. In 2027, the Italian team will launch its inaugural full-season GTD campaign. They will field the No. 50 Ferrari 296 GT3 EVO across the entire schedule. This move comes after the team won the 2025 GTD title and secured six WeatherTech Championship wins. The plan includes a second car, the No. 21, reserved for the Rolex 24 At Daytona. Matias Perez Companc and Nicklas Nielsen will drive the full season in the No. 50 entry, according to Sportscar365 . The team made this announcement on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. The shift to a full season shows a major commitment to the American series. It builds on a history of strong endurance racing results. Lilou Wadoux will join for the Michelin Endurance Cup rounds. Arthur Leclerc completes the four-driver roster for the season opener in Florida. This lineup brings together experienced racers and official factory drivers. A New Era for the No. 50 Ferrari The core of this effort is the partnership between Matias Perez Companc and Nicklas Nielsen. Perez Companc has a deep history with the program. He competed in the GT World Challenge America Pro class last season. He and Frederik Schandorff won an overall race at Barber Motorsports Park in September. Nielsen brings his own experience to the seat. He raced in the team’s Hypercar program for the FIA World Endurance Championship over the last two seasons. The car itself is the Ferrari 296 GT3 EVO. This machine sits at the heart of the North American program. According to the team, it stands prepared to tackle the challenges inherent in IMSA competition. They will start with the legendary 24 Hours of Daytona. The full-season GTD program will run in the traditional blue livery of the Perez Companc family. This visual identity has been a staple for the team. The expansion signals that AF Corse plans to stay for the long haul. Star Power for the Rolex 24 The Rolex 24 At Daytona will feature a second entry in GTD Pro. The No. 21 Ferrari 296 GT3 EVO will feature the classic rosso red livery. Four drivers will share the wheel for this one-off effort. Simon Mann leads the group. Since 2021, he has consistently competed in the No. 21 Ferrari. At the March Mobil 1 Twelve Hours of Sebring, Mann assisted the team in claiming a GTD victory. His 25th career IMSA start will occur at Daytona. Alec Udell is the lone American among the eight drivers in the two cars. He brings 26 WeatherTech Championship starts, the most of the group. His best finish is a second place at Lime Rock Park in 2023. Tommaso Mosca returns after finishing fifth in the No. 21 entry at the 2026 Rolex 24. Most of the leaves are off of most of the trees, the squeaks of sneakers on linoleum is ringing through fieldhouses around the state and, this week at least, plates are looking almost as full as Indiana football’s trophy case. Todd Yeagley has another great group on his hands and turned some strong development and offseason moves into winning the Big Ten double this season. The longtime staple, an absolute treat during the winter months, closed its doors years ago largely due to a drop in traffic from the COVID-19 pandemic. Following the Phoenix Suns ’ 116-104 loss to the Houston Rockets during NBA Cup play Wednesday night, forward Dillon Brooks addressed his heated exchange with Kevin Durant that resulted in his ejection in the closing seconds of the game. item.title: Milan fight back to beat Olympiacos in Europa League
item.description: FILE PHOTO - The UEFA Europa League logo is pictured at the Europa-Park Stadium. (is associated with: «Milan fight back to beat Olympiacos in Europa League») Harry Langer/dpa AC Milan produced a second-half fightback from 2-0 down to beat Olympiacos 4-2 in Piraeus and kick-start their Europa League campaign. After a low-key start at the Stadio Georgios Karaiskakis, Olympiacos broke the deadlock from a corner in the 31st minute. Former Inter defender Lorenzo Pirola crashed a header against the crossbar and the ball bounced back into the net off Mike Maignan’s arm. Milan – who had lost three of their four previous Europa League games – were close to a swift equalizer in the 35th minute. Alphadjo Cisse raced onto a through pass as Olympiacos keeper Stefan Ortega rushed out, and then stabbed the loose ball goalwards only for Pirola to hack it clear as he slid on into a post. Pirola then missed a chance to double Olympiacos’ lead in stoppage time at the end of the first half when he fired over from 10 yards. Olympiacos, who were unbeaten in Europe with three wins, scored again four minutes into the second half. Remo Freuler found Jota Silva at the edge of the penalty area and he fired the ball past Maignan into the top corner. Milan got themselves back into the match through a fine individual goal from Omari Hutchinson in the 56th minute. The on-loan Nottingham Forest winger picked the ball up on the halfway line and burst down the right before cutting inside at the edge of the penalty area and rolling the ball into the far corner. The Rossoneri struck again in the 63rd minute when Hutchinson sent over a floated cross from the right towards the back post where Cisse nodded the ball past Ortega. Substitute Christian Pulisic completed the turnaround with 20 minutes left when he volleyed home a cross from the right after more quick footwork from Hutchinson. Diego Moreira swept home a fourth in added time following a swift counterattack by Pulisic.

item.title: Rayan fires 10-man Bournemouth to Europa League victory at Celta Vigo
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Bournemouth manager Marco Rose salutes the fans following the English Premier League soccer match between AFC Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest at Vitality Stadium. (is associated with: «Rayan fires 10-man Bournemouth to Europa League victory at Celta Vigo») Steven Paston/PA Wire/dpa Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo. It was a remarkable 10th victory in a row in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time. The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Bafode Diakite was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle. Bournemouth might have folded then, but instead they came roaring back, Alvaro Rodriguez heading them level almost immediately after the start of the second half. A draw would have been an excellent result in the circumstances. Substitute Rayan had other ideas, waiting at the end of a rapid breakaway to sweep in the winner 12 minutes from time. Victory against Viktoria Plzen in December will almost certainly now be enough to earn direct passage to the last 16.

item.title: Ibrahim Osman stars as Brighton bounce back with Conference League win
item.description: Brighton and Hove Albion's Charalampos Kostoulas celebrates scoring his side's third goal during the UEFA Europa Conference League soccer match between Brighton and Hove Albion and CS Universitatea Craiova at the American Express Stadium. (is associated with: «Ibrahim Osman stars as Brighton bounce back with Conference League win») Gareth Fuller/PA Wire/dpa Ibrahim Osman scored his first Brighton goals as his side returned to winning ways by cruising to a 4-0 success over 10-man Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League. Talk of the high-flying Seagulls potentially being shock Premier League title contenders this season was dampened slightly by Sunday’s surprise 2-0 defeat at Hull. Winger Osman finished a flowing move to set Albion on course to avoid a further unexpected defeat before Maxim De Cuyper superbly curled home his fifth goal of the campaign to double the lead. Romanian champions Craiova were left with little hope of a comeback at the Amex Stadium when defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off in the 39th minute for stamping on the ankle of Matt O’Riley. Osman set up Charalampos Kostoulas for the third goal before quickly claiming his second with a fine individual effort as Brighton made it 10 points from four games in the competition on a bitterly cold evening in Sussex.

On this note, I’d like to share with you a thought that has been bouncing around in my head for years: most ballplayers’ walk-up songs are terrible. And no, this thought is not an old man shakes his fist at cloud moment. While most ballparks have noise that sort of blends into each other (and Dodger Stadium is a prime example), as I have said elsewhere lately, there is a better way. New Canaan forced two turnovers which led to touchdowns in the first 3:05 and rolled to its ninth consecutive Turkey Bowl victory 33-13 over Darien Thursday in Darien. The No. 4-ranked Rams (8-2) had already unofficially secured a Class L tournament berth before the game, but the victory secured a home game for the quarterfinals, which are set for Tuesday. Darien (6-4) can still qualify for the Class L playoffs, but would need bonus points to fall its way. New Canaan's defense was in takeaway mode in the first few minutes. On the second play from scrimmage, a hit by Spencer Schaefer forced a fumble and Thomas Tchakarov recovered at the Darien 22-yard line. Three plays later, Jack Crowell scored on a six-yard run for a 7-0 lead. On the Blue Wave's next possession, Dallas George intercepted a High Dunlop pass and set New Canaan up at the Darien four-yard line. George then carried it in for a four-yard touchdown run and an early 14-0 lead. Kicker Neel Arora followed with field goals of 32 and 35 yards, and a blocked punt by Jack Nicolet led to a 13-yard return by George and the Rams had a 27-0 lead at halftime. The Rams retained the Coaches Memorial Trophy, dedicated in honor of former coaches John Maher of Darien (1945–65) and Joe Sikorski of New Canaan (1949-1969). New Canaan has qualified for the CIAC playoffs for 21 consecutive seasons, a run which started in 2005 when Curt Casali was a junior quarterback. Casali spent 11 years as an MLB catcher, retiring in 2024. The Rams have also won 12 of the last 13 contests with Darien, including in the 2023 and 2024 Class L finals. Darien's lone win during that stretch was in the 2021 Class LL semis and the Wave went on to win the championship that year. Overall in the rivalry, New Canaan now has a 62-39-2 lead, with a 22-9-1 advantage on Thanksgiving. item.title: Mason Posa on Minnesota rivalry: ‘I hate looking at them’
item.description: COLLEGE PARK, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 14: Mason Posa #8 of the Wisconsin Badgers lines up against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium on November 14, 2026 in College Park, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images In college football, with as much change as we’ve seen over the past few years, there have been questions about whether rivalries still mean as much as they do, given that players have constantly changed schools. Just don’t tell that to Wisconsin Badgers star Mason Posa, who clearly didn’t get the memo. Ahead of this weekend’s matchup against the Minnesota Gophers, the sophomore linebacker didn’t mince words when talking about his opponent. “Yeah, no, it means everything to me,” Posa said about winning this weekend. “I’m kind of losing sleep a little bit just thinking about the game. Just, you know, I really want to beat these guys. And this is a team I can’t stand. I hate looking at them. I hate hearing their name. And, you know, it’s going to be a fun game to play. “And they’re a good football team too. They got good players. They’ve had some really good games, some close games. And they could come at us any other way. So we got to be prepared. And, you know, just really excited to play.” Posa has played with his heart on his sleeve all season long, and the Badgers defense has certainly benefited from it. The star linebacker was recently listed as a finalist for the Butkus Award, given to the best linebacker in the country. Wisconsin is looking to snap a two-game losing streak to the Gophers, who have won four of the last five matchups. The Badgers would also reach eight wins for the first time under Luke Fickell, whose job security has been a hot topic over the past month. So, there’s a lot at stake for Wisconsin, and the pressure is on them heading into the key rivalry game.

item.title: Ohio State gets more bad news as criticism mounts for Ryan Day
item.description: An Ohio State Buckeyes helmet sits behind the endzone as the team warms up for its game against the Michigan Wolverines during the NCAA football game at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, Mich. on Nov. 29, 2025. Ohio State won 27-9. It’s been a rough few weeks for the Ohio State Buckeyes and head coach Ryan Day. Ohio State has dropped three of its last four games and fallen out of the College Football Playoff picture, and the pressure on Day has only continued to grow heading into Saturday’s game against the Michigan Wolverines. Now, things have gotten even worse. Five-star edge rusher David “DJ” Jacobs, one of the top recruits in the country, has decommitted from Ohio State on Thanksgiving, just two days before the Buckeyes’ rivalry game and days before the early signing period. Ohio State’s Disappointing Season The Buckeyes entered the season with national championship expectations, but they’ve stumbled to a 7-4 record. Ohio State lost to Texas in Week 2, then fell to USC, Oregon, and Nebraska after star quarterback Julian Sayin suffered a season-ending arm injury. The criticism has been coming from everywhere. Ohio State legend Cris Carter ripped the program this week, questioning the communication within the coaching staff and saying that “the film looks like we ain’t got no heart.” Some Buckeye fans have already laid out the case for firing Day , pointing to the program’s failures in player development and game management. And with Michigan coming to Columbus on Saturday, Day’s seat is only going to get hotter if the Buckeyes lose. Jacobs Decommits On Thursday afternoon, national recruiting reporter Hayes Fawcett broke the news that Jacobs had backed off his commitment from Ohio State. “BREAKING: Five-Star Plus+ EDGE David ‘DJ’ Jacobs has Decommitted from Ohio State, he tells me for @Rivals. He’s ranked as the No. 1 Recruit in the 2027 Class,” Fawcett wrote . Jacobs, a 6-foot-5 edge rusher from Blessed Trinity Catholic in Roswell, Georgia, is the top-ranked edge rusher in the 2027 class and the No. 2 overall prospect in the 247Sports composite. He was the crown jewel of Ohio State’s 2027 class. Jacobs committed to the Buckeyes last December, announcing his decision on live television just days before Ohio State’s College Football Playoff quarterfinal against Miami. He picked Ohio State over a long list of suitors, including Georgia, where his father played, as well as Miami and Texas A&M. Tennessee and Georgia have continued to pursue him throughout his commitment, and both are expected to be in the mix now that his recruitment is back open. Needless to say, losing the top recruit in the country on Thanksgiving is about the last thing Day needed heading into The Game. item.title: 3 storylines for Alabama vs. Auburn in Iron Bowl showdown
item.description: On Saturday night, one of college football's premier annual rivalries will be renewed when Alabama hosts Auburn for the latest chapter of the Iron Bowl. A storied matchup between two in-state foes, the Crimson Tide have faced Auburn countless times before with high stakes attached, with some of the biggest meetings coming during the Nick Saban era. That has carried over to the Kalen DeBoer era, with this latest matchup once again featuring high stakes for the Crimson Tide in particular. Alabama will enter the Iron Bowl ranked No. 6 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings , as well as still in the mix for a trip to the SEC Championship Game. As a result, when it comes to making the playoff, all the Tide have to do is win and they are in. Following are three storylines to watch for Saturday night when Alabama and Auburn collide in the latest Iron Bowl. Will Alabama continue recent Iron Bowl success in Tuscaloosa? Not only has Alabama won the last six games against Auburn dating back to the 2020 season, but the Crimson Tide have also owned the recent series in Tuscaloosa winning the last seven, with each game's margin of victory coming by double digits. The last Auburn team to win in Tuscaloosa was the Tigers' 2010 national title winning squad led by Heisman Trophy winning quarterback Cam Newton. Auburn won that game with a second half comeback, 28-27. Can Alabama's defense contain Byrum Brown? Saturday will mark the third time Alabama's defense has faced Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown in his career, with the former USF transfer having torched the Tide on the ground with 200 rushing yards in two prior games, despite struggling as a passer. Brown is certain to provide challenges for the Tide's defense again Saturday when running the ball, and will likely need to see success on the ground as Auburn's leading rusher has been hurt at times this season by turnovers, throwing eight picks. Can Alabama's pass rush take advantage of Auburn offensive line? Alabama's defensive front will be facing an Auburn offensive line that has struggled to protect the quarterback this season, with the Tigers currently ranking among the worst in FBS with 39 sacks allowed over 11 games. Alabama is tied for the fifth-most sacks in the SEC this season with 31, and have racked up a combined 13 during their current four-game winning streak. item.title: Eight Short Game Shots Define Scoring Mastery For Serious Golfers
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images A solid short game turns a bad round into a great one by saving strokes inside 80 yards. Golf Monthly identifies eight key shots every player must master to handle sand, rough, and slopes. These include the chip-and-run, chip-pitch, pitch, bunker shot, hybrid bunt, flop, upslope or downslope play, and a shot from the rough. The chip-and-run is the starting point for any good short game when obstacles are absent. According to reports, the shot allows the ball to start rolling earlier and leaves a large amount of green ahead. This method is the safest and most predictable way to knock the ball near the hole. Players should grip down the shaft and stand closer to the ball with 70% of their weight on the front foot. The Chip-Pitch And Pitch Shots When a player needs more carry than a chip but less speed than a full shot, the chip-pitch becomes the answer. This shot works well when a golfer is around 20 yards off the green and has room for the ball to release upon landing. The setup mirrors the chip-and-run but requires a slightly different feel to get the ball airborne without losing control. A standard pitch shot offers even higher flight and more distance. The motion involves more wrist action than the chip, allowing the player to stop the ball quickly on the green. Davies proposes visualizing wrist cock on a zero to five scale, with five indicating the maximum usage for a flop shot. Bunker And Hybrid Bunt Techniques Bunker play requires a specific technique to escape sand without losing distance or direction. The hybrid bunt can be used when a standard wedge does not work. The flop shot demands the most wrist action and is used to get the ball high and soft over an obstacle. It is the most difficult shot on the list and requires a precise touch to avoid hitting it too far or too short. Players must feel the clubhead slide under the ball while keeping their hands ahead of the clubhead at impact. Dealing With Slopes And Rough Slopes affect play, requiring players to adjust their aim and club selection for upslope or downslope lies. A shot from the rough adds another layer of difficulty as thick grass grabs the clubface and reduces spin. Converting three or four shots down to two elevates a player’s game to the next level. Davies stresses that sharp play from inside 80 yards lets a golfer exploit par 5s and short par 4s. The top five finishers at the Final Stage of PGA Tour Q School will earn membership for 2027.

item.title: Five things we learned from Barcelona’s 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League
item.description: Five things we learned from Barcelona’s 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League Barcelona secured their fourth victory in the league phase of the UEFA Champions League last night, beating Sabah 4-1 away in Baku. The game was a real eye-opener for Hansi Flick for multiple reasons, including the performances of new summer signings as well as the debut of Alex Campos, among others. This comes just in time for Flick as Barcelona gear up for a gruelling December schedule that is going to test the depth of this squad. Here, we will take a look at five things we learnt from Barcelona’s win over Sabah this midweek. Alex Campos looks like a promising talent Campos’ debut performance was indeed one of the highlights in Barcelona’s win over Sabah as the youngster produced a solid cameo in the last 27 minutes of the game. The teenager looked composed on the ball and offered a lot of technical quality when playing out from the back. His maturity, coupled with his versatility, could make an ideal in-house solution for Barcelona’s defensive problem heading into the December period. Campos can indeed operate as the extra central defensive option at a time when the majority of the defence has either struggled with fitness or has been forced to play elsewhere. Balde deserves more opportunities Alejandro Balde made an impression on his rare start. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) Alejandro Balde made a rare appearance against Sabah in the left-back position, having largely spent the season on the bench. The Spaniard didn’t disappoint either and reminded everyone what he can offer to the table. His marauding runs caused problems for the Sabah defence while adding more width to the Barcelona frontline. It allowed Anthony Gordon to operate more centrally as well. Balde notably mustered a brilliant assist for Karim Adeyemi’s goal, but picked up a knock . However, he has not been completely ruled out for the upcoming Deportivo clash. Adeyemi, Gordon and Gabriel Jesus needed this The real stars of the game were Barcelona’s three offensive signings of the summer in Gabriel Jesus, Gordon and Adeyemi. The trio delivered four goals on the night, barely letting Barcelona feel the absence of their star duo Raphinha and Lamine Yamal. Their collective performance is a good sign for Barcelona heading into the December period. item.title: Former Atletico Madrid star defends Vinicius amid Real Madrid criticism: ‘If he scores 24 goals…’
item.description: Former Atletico Madrid star defends Vinicius amid Real Madrid criticism: ‘If he scores 24 goals…’ Vinicius Jr.’s goal was the biggest takeaway for Real Madrid as they secured a thumping 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League this midweek. The Brazilian scored the final goal of the game for Los Blancos . It was also his first goal for Real Madrid in three months, in what has been an underwhelming start to the season for the Brazilian. Although Vinicius has shown early signs of improvement of late, there is still widespread criticism over his performances and whether or not he deserves a place in the starting eleven. Mario Suarez on Vinicius Jr. While Real Madrid remain determined to help Vinicius Jr. get back to full form , former Atletico Madrid player Mario Suarez has offered his two cents on his situation. Vinicius Jr. has scored only two goals this season. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) A one-time Spanish champion with Atleti, Suarez talked about criticism surrounding Vinicius’ goal output, especially in relation to recent praise for Yan Diomande’s defensive work rate. “Football is what it is. Vinicius plays great games many times and, if he doesn’t score goals, he gets criticised. Now it’s praised that Diomande defends more than him,” he told COPE (h/t Defensa Central ). “If Vinicius scores 24 goals from now until the end of the season and Diomande scores 10, however much he defends, Vinicius will be praised more than Diomande. Football is like that and it’s all been invented,” he added. Suarez effectively means that attacking players are judged mainly on their end product, and the same is the case for Vinicius., who won’t be judged at the end of the season based on how much defensive work he puts in. A crucial month ahead for Vini and Diomande Suarez’s comment comes at a time when both Vinicius and Diomande are currently vying for a starting place in the Real Madrid eleven. Vinicius and Diomande are locked in a battle for the starting eleven. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Although Jose Mourinho was able to start both in the same lineup against PSV Eindhoven, it won’t be the case against other opponents, especially when Los Blancos will require a stronger midfield. Vinicius, therefore, will be hoping to capitalise on the early green shoots and continue the momentum into December, when Mourinho will be forced to make rotations due to a congested schedule. For now, though, Diomande may be slightly ahead in the pecking order, having performed brilliantly since the end of the first international break. The Ivorian, though, hasn’t scored in the last four matches so Mourinho himself will have to make some tough decisions in the coming weeks.

item.title: Dricus du Plessis claims UFC shot down Khamzat Chimaev rematch
item.description: Dricus du Plessis and Khamzat Chimaev fought at UFC 319 | Ed Mulholland, Zuffa LLC Dricus du Plessis has been on the hunt for another fight with Khamzat Chimaev, even if the UFC isn’t interested for now. Chimaev defeated du Plessis at UFC 319 to become middleweight champion, only to subsequently lose the title to Sean Strickland at UFC 328. While Chimaev and Strickland settled their business, du Plessis returned to action at UFC Oklahoma City in July to pick up a five-round decision win over former welterweight champion Kamaru Usman. That performance kept du Plessis in the contender picture, which is currently murky with Strickland’s next title defense still to be announced, and Chimaev teasing a move up to light heavyweight while also keeping Strickland in his sights. Du Plessis told Fight Forecast he wanted a rematch with Chimaev, but has so far been denied. “I’ve asked for Khamzat now,” du Plessis said. “I asked for that fight. We said we want that fight and they said, no, they don’t want to do that right now. I said if that’s the next fight they want to make, I’m definitely keen. I’m definitely keen for that fight again. Believe me, he’s not fighting the same guy that he fought that night.” Du Plessis lost a disappointing decision to Chimaev as he struggled to deal with Chimaev’s wrestling for almost the entirety of their fight. He showed improvements in his wrestling defense against Usman, stopping all seven of his takedown attempts (per UFC Stats ). As much as he wants to avenge the Chimaev loss, du Plessis is always open to fighting Strickland again as well. Du Plessis is currently up 2-0 in their series, having won a razor-close split decision at UFC 297 to become champion and then winning another decision in their rematch at UFC 312. He expects a third fight to go the same way. “Absolutely, for me, like I always say, I want to fight for the belt,” du Plessis said when asked if he’s interested in a Strickland trilogy. “If he has the belt, that’s the guy I’m fighting. If that’s what needs to happen, that’s what I’ll do. “Kryptonite. That’s it, some guys just have another guy’s number and that’s it.” Du Plessis has recently been teasing fight news and though he still can’t make any official announcement, he expects his next opponent to be revealed soon. “I want to fight,” du Plessis said. “I said I’ll be ready to fight in February, but we’ve agreed to a fight. Me and the UFC, we’ve come to an agreement, and the big news will be out soon. I’m really happy to announce finally. The next fight, it’s not signed, but I’ve confirmed.”

item.description: (Photo by S. Mellar/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images As an outsider, one cannot evaluate Jamal Musiala’s personal life and can only make ill-advised assumptions. But it is clear that Musiala’s professional career has suffered greatly over the last 19 months. He was diagnosed with terrifying absence seizures in April 2025 before injury added insult to injury, with first a muscular injury and then a fractured fibula keeping him out of action. Even after his fibula healed, repeated muscle injuries have ensured that the 23-year-old has not played five games in a row since his absence seizure diagnosis. How awful it must be to have to learn to cope with such a neurological condition while being consistently robbed of one of the greatest joys of one’s life—playing football. How can someone come back from this? Bayern’s vice captain, Joshua Kimmich, has witnessed most of his journey, though, and is not plagued by any doubts. Asked how confident he is that Musiala will return to his usual level, Bayern’s No. 6 made his thoughts very clear: “100 percent. As I just said, I think the important thing for him now is to get a few games under his belt in succession so that he can find his rhythm again. Of course, there’s a certain amount of pressure on him because expectations are high, and he also expects a lot from himself. You sometimes think you can come back in and immediately decide games,” Kimmich admitte d (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), before explaining why this line of thinking is simply not realistic. “I do n’t think we should expect miracles right now, and that’s not just the case with Jamal but also with all the other injured players who will eventually return. item.title: Ford’s New GT41 Hypercar Revives Its Le Mans Rivalry With Ferrari
item.description: 2027 Ford GT41 Le Mans Hypercar: What We Know Frank Markus - MotorTrend Ford has declared itself “America’s Racing Team.” Whadabout Haas and Cadillac? Those two each campaign cars in Formula 1. Or the American Racing Team? Well, the former two don’t compete across as many series, and latter only competes on two wheels in Moto2. Ford’s case for claiming the America’s Team title is that it competes on the world stage in loads of series—the FIA World Endurance Championship and IMSA GT3-spec GTD classes, GT World Challenge, DTM, and the Asian Le Mans Series. And in F1, it’s a technical partner in Red Bull-Ford Powertrains. The Blue Oval also runs in the SCORE Baja racing category. And Ford in 2027 will again return to the WEC’s Hypercar ranks—the top class in Le Mans–style sports car racing. Ford Ford’s Le Mans History Even moviegoing casual motorsports followers know Ford campaigned GT40s at Le Mans from 1964 through 1967, vanquishing Enzo Ferrari’s best in 1966 while competing in the series’ top Prototype P +5.0 class, running 427-cubic-inch engines. Then privateers in GT40s took the overall Le Mans wins in 1968 and ’69 campaigning 4.9-liter GT40s in a homologated Group 4 Sports Car class. Ford returned in 2016, entering a twin-turbo V-6-powered GT and winning a similar homologated road car class in the French endurance race, LMGTE Pro. But did you know that a Ford competed in the very first Le Mans race in 1923? French Ford dealer Charles Montier drove a Model T for 97 laps, averaging 43.4 mph, to finish seventh in class and 14th overall. Preproduction vehicle. Not available for purchase. Ford LMDh This Time Around In celebration of the 60th anniversary of its big 1-2-3 Le Mans achievement, Ford will in 2027 once again contend for the overall win in the series’ top Hypercar class, competing directly against Ferrari. Except the historic rivals are designing their Hypercars according to slightly different rules. To contain costs, Ford is running in LMDh (Le Mans Daytona hybrid), which must utilize one of four spec chassis (Ford has chosen ORECA; the others are supplied by Dallara, Ligier, and Multimatic). The hybrid system is also a spec unit, consisting of a Williams Advanced Engineering (WAE) battery pack powering a 50-kW Bosch motor-generator unit integrated into an Xtrac seven-speed sequential gearbox. Ford is fully responsible for the engine design and development and full integration of the entire powertrain, chassis, body, and aerodynamics. Ferrari competes in LMH (Le Mans Hypercar) and is therefore free to develop its own chassis, engine, and hybrid system. An important difference: LMH allows up to 200 kW (268 hp) applied at the front axle—but only at speeds too high to help with corner exits, and the maximum delivered to all four wheels still can’t exceed a maximum allowable total output. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
